title: Manage permitted user access and region scope
summary: Understand permitted Region Scope changes and Subregion boundary operations.

evidence: server/src/utils/guideOracleKnowledge.js: reviewed original fact objects at b8345be4d2f7a097e81cb03eef64b473abd0cec9

sections.title: Review a permitted platform-role change for another account
paragraphs: Only Super Admin can change platform roles through the current Users table, and cannot change their own role. A platform role is separate from Place/Offering assignments and organisation or group access.
steps: As an authorised Super Admin, open Dashboard → Admin → Users and find the exact account.
Check the intended account identity and current role before touching the role selector. Do not use personal profile details beyond what is needed for this authorised task.

Choose the approved next role from that account’s available role selector only when ready to apply it. Selecting a role starts the saved update immediately; there is no later Save button for this table action.
Wait for the refreshed Users table and verify the saved role. If the change fails, review the reported error and current role before retrying.
notes: The server checks the target account, allowable role and relevant manager compatibility. A job title is not an account role and cannot establish a permission.
A role change does not by itself create a resource Owner/Staff assignment, organisation membership or group membership. Review each permitted access domain separately.
If the role selector is unavailable, do not substitute another account or a hidden route. Ask the responsible Super Admin for review.
The Guide cannot change another account’s role or inspect its private assignment records in chat.

sections.title: Review and save an Admin’s assigned Region Scope
paragraphs: Only Super Admin can assign Region Scope to an Admin account. This controls scoped administrative work; it does not grant resource editing, organisation access or group access.
steps: Open Dashboard → Admin → Users and find the exact Admin account.
Select that account’s Manage Region Scope control and verify the target shown in the dialog.
Review Assigned Region Scope and select the intended Subregions. Select all and Clear change the pending selection, so review the resulting set carefully.
Check that the Admin’s managed users remain within the proposed scope before saving. If that would not be true, arrange the appropriate approved user-management change first.
Select Save Region Scope and wait for Region scope updated. Check the saved selections; use Cancel or Close to leave an unsaved selection.
If the server blocks the change, review the reported out-of-scope users and approved reassignment plan. Do not remove boundaries simply to bypass the validation.
notes: The UI’s Region Scope targets operational Subregions. It is distinct from a person’s profile postal code or general support coverage.
A signed-in Admin can ask the Guide for this account’s current assigned Subregions. The Guide cannot show or change another account’s scope in chat.
Keep user names, postal details and scope screenshots within authorised operational channels. This procedure does not require sharing credentials or private profile values.

sections.title: Export and review permitted Subregion boundaries before an upload
paragraphs: Super Admin can maintain Subregion metadata. An Admin can upload or export boundary postcodes only inside their assigned scope. Regions, operational Subregions and Unmapped postcodes are separate layers; account/resource routing uses Subregion postcodes.
steps: Open Dashboard → Admin → Regions and inspect the Boundary Layers and relevant Subregions. Verify the operational layer and scope you intend to change.
Select the intended Subregions and use Export Boundaries to review their current postcodes. Use Boundary Template to prepare a correctly structured CSV or Excel upload.
Review the file’s Subregion references and postal codes or ranges against the approved change. Keep Add to existing boundaries selected when adding codes to the existing boundaries.
Select Upload Boundaries and choose the reviewed file only when ready for the import. For Add to existing boundaries, upload begins processing without a separate replacement confirmation.

For an approved planned rebuild only, choose Replace listed subregions before the upload. Read Replace existing boundaries? and explicitly choose Replace only when the removal-and-rebuild scope is intended; Cancel stops that replacement.
Wait for the outcome and review successful/failed counts and errors. Export the affected boundaries again to verify the intended result before relying on the changed routing.
notes: Replace listed subregions removes existing codes for affected Subregions first. It is not the default add operation, and files too large for the permitted single replacement upload are rejected; review a planned rebuild rather than blindly retrying.
Subregion names, codes, metadata changes and deletion remain Super Admin controls. Uploading boundaries does not grant a wider Admin scope.

Load mapping workbook is a separate Super Admin three-layer operation using the mapping workbook’s postal/Region/Subregion columns. Do not treat it as a substitute for a small additive boundary upload.
A failed or partially successful report does not prove all boundaries changed. Review the report and actual exported result before proceeding.
The Guide cannot upload, replace or inspect current mapping records in chat. Keep exports and operational mapping details in authorised channels.

facts.title: Admin Region Scope
keywords: which regions can an admin manage
facts.message: Region Scope assigns Subregions to an Admin account. A Super Admin can open Admin → Users, choose the exact Admin, then use Manage Region Scope to review and save its assigned Subregions. The server checks the current roles and prevents a scope change that would leave that Admin’s managed users outside the new scope. Region Scope controls scoped admin work; it does not grant editing of a Place or Programme/service, organisation access, or group access. A signed-in Admin can ask the Guide for this account’s current assigned Subregions; the Guide cannot show or change another account’s assignment in chat.

facts.title: Regions and Subregion boundaries
facts.message: Admin → Regions shows three separate layers: Regions, operational Subregions, and Unmapped postcodes awaiting review. Only Subregion postcodes route accounts and resources. Super Admin can create or change Subregion metadata and load the three-layer mapping workbook. An Admin can upload or export boundary postcodes only for Subregions within their assigned scope; names, codes and deletion remain Super Admin controls. Upload Boundaries defaults to Add to existing boundaries. Replace listed subregions removes existing codes for affected Subregions first, so use it only for a planned rebuild after reviewing the file and confirmation. The Guide cannot inspect current mappings or upload or replace boundaries in chat.
